- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast to avoid overreaction.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment is positive — cap forecast rise to 5-7% above recent peak.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in strong trends — if price moves >10% from 10-day average, adjust forecast downward by 1-3% per day until reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently misses late-period momentum — if sentiment turns positive after day 15, increase forecast tail (last 5 days) by 1-2% to capture rally.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often lags — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to catch momentum.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes — if sentiment jumps to 1.00, don’t increase forecast by >3% unless confirmed by 2+ consecutive days.
